1.explanation: The empty /**/ is currently being matched by the JSDOC_COMMENT mode (defined in javascript.js) instead of the generic C_BLOCK_COMMENT_MODE. JSDOC_COMMENT begins on '/**' and ends on '*/', but its internal configuration (contains doctag rules only) doesn’t handle a zero-length body, leaving the parser stuck inside a comment mode. The COMMENT variant groups together JSDOC_COMMENT and C_BLOCK_COMMENT_MODE, but because JSDOC_COMMENT is listed first, it always wins on '/**/', preventing normal code parsing from resuming. The default export function in javascript.js is where these modes are wired up, and compileLanguage in mode_compiler.js is responsible for building the underlying regex machinery that executes the begin/end logic. Fixing this requires adjusting the JSDOC_COMMENT definition (or its priority) so that an empty '/**/' is treated as a standard block comment (or explicitly allowed) and doesn’t block further highlighting.
1.bug_scenario: When using highlight (not highlightAuto) on a JavaScript snippet that starts and ends with an empty block comment (/**/console.log("Hello, World!")/**/), the highlighter treats the initial /**/ as the start of a JSDoc-style comment and never correctly resumes highlighting the code or the trailing /**/. The code after the first empty /**/ is shown as plain text (no coloring), and the final /**/ is also not recognized.

2.explanation: The two mode definitions in javascript.js control how /*…*/-style comments are recognized. JSDOC_COMMENT is defined to begin on '/**' and end on '*/' and lives ahead of the generic C_BLOCK_COMMENT_MODE inside the COMMENT variants. Because it will happily match an empty '/**/’ it enters comment mode and never hands control back to the lexer for the code that follows. By adjusting JSDOC_COMMENT (for example, requiring at least one non-asterisk inside, or changing the order so that empty block comments are handled by the simpler C_BLOCK_COMMENT_MODE and immediately exited) or by modifying the COMMENT variant list, you can prevent an empty /**/ from halting further highlighting. The default export function wraps these modes into the language definition, so any change to how COMMENT or JSDOC_COMMENT is built must happen before or inside that function.
2.bug_scenario: When you put an empty block comment at the very start of a JavaScript snippet—e.g. “/**/console.log(…)/**/”—highlight.js will consume the first “/**/” as a JSDoc comment and never resume normal tokenization, so none of the console.log call or the trailing “/**/” get highlighted. In other words, the empty comment mode “locks up” the parser and breaks all subsequent syntax highlighting.
